author: hangleang
content: I have a few questions on builder blacklisting design while implementing along side the circuit breaker. (1) should blacklisted builders' bid be propagated or forwarded to our peers? (2) what payload status should be consider its builder to be blacklisted? is the decision based on local view or PTC votes?

author: nflaig
content: gonna answer this so that potuz can correct my wrong response later, so for (1) I think we should not apply this to p2p bids at all, only for direct builders, and (2) if the block was strong and payload was not revealed it should be counted as a fault

author: hangleang
content: Agree for (1) we should accept and forward, but also filter out their bids from value comparison (highest bid), otherwise they can suppress honest builders from acceptance

author: potuz
content: Terence also agrees with you but I implemented dropping bids from blacklisted builders and not propagating them. The rationale was that if we blacklist a builder is because we think it's a danger for the chain and therefore we shouldn't propagate that bid. I'm willing to change that view though. Cc <@363800010518822915> I should have taken your bet: it wasn't AI that found about this 🙂

author: nflaig
content:
> therefore we shouldn't propagate that bid
shouldn't the circuit breaker stay local only and not affect p2p propagation, or otherwise should this be part of the spec? anyways I feel like this is pointless, p2p bids can be sybil attacked easily, so using builder pubkey/index to blacklist doesn't make sense. I am mean sure you can do that but I wouldn't add this if it adds extra complexity
